items.title: Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT's new biology skills wow scientists
items.excerpt: Anthropic and OpenAI's general-purpose language models can now design proteins and predict their sequences and structures, abilities previously seen only in specialized tools such as AlphaFold. OpenAI reports 35 of 322 GPT-6.2 protein designs bound five targets in lab tests (about 10.9%).

items.title: A long-context generative foundation model for versatile RNA design (EVA)
items.excerpt: Huang, Lv, Gao and colleagues study RNA scaling laws and introduce EVA, a long-context RNA foundation model for function prediction and diverse RNA design. The paper includes experimental validation of designed functional RNAs.

items.title: De novo identification of protein domains in cryo-electron tomography maps from AlphaFold2 models (DomainSeeker)
items.excerpt: Identifying proteins in medium- to low-resolution cryo-electron tomography density maps is hard. The authors develop DomainSeeker, which combines AlphaFold2 models with experimental data to identify protein domains directly from in-situ density maps.

items.title: AI helps chemists design the next generation of artificial enzymes (molecular cage catalysts)
items.excerpt: Oxford researchers trained machine learning on reaction-rate data, using cage shape, size, volume and electrostatics to predict the catalytic activity of enzyme-like molecular cages (JACS). Edinburgh researchers then assembled and tested 30 palladium cages in a rapid in-solution screen, and their activity varied by more than 10,000-fold.

items.title: AI-assisted method advances high-resolution structure classification of membrane proteins in vesicles
items.excerpt: An AI model from the CAS Institute of Biophysics estimates vesicle membrane geometry by fitting ellipsoidal surfaces, then filters cryo-EM particles. It reconstructed vesicle-embedded membrane proteins at 2.7 A (influenza hemagglutinin) and 3.1 A (OC43 spike) (PNAS).

items.title: AI-designed protein tricks defective insulin receptors into working in new mouse study
items.excerpt: Scientists report that an AI-designed protein activates broken insulin receptors in lab mice. The result hints at a possible new treatment for some severe forms of insulin resistance (medicine boundary: disease-targeted).

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.excerpt: Teams of Gemini 4 agents improved well-known quantum algorithms by sharing ideas in periodic virtual meetings, and the Lean theorem prover formally verified each result. Gains include an 11.8x cost cut for a fusion-related calculation, a 2.57x Grover speedup and a 290x arcsin speedup (arXiv:2611.09822).

items.title: Neural Network Decoders For Qubit Loss
items.excerpt: Qubit loss is a major error source on neutral-atom and other platforms, and loss-resolving measurements can cut fault-tolerance overhead. Staples, Fu, Dong and Thompson train neural-network decoders that use loss information for the surface code, getting around the cost of simulating and decoding loss outside the stabilizer framework.

items.title: Neural Decoding of Logical Clifford Circuits with Transversal Gates (Duet)
items.excerpt: Transversal gates on neutral-atom and trapped-ion machines make logical gates up to d times faster but spread errors across blocks, which makes decoding harder. Duet is a neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits that builds in the known error propagation, and the authors release its code and trained networks.

items.title: Towards three-dimensional dark matter mapping in the extended solar neighbourhood with Gaia DR3 and deep learning
items.excerpt: Kim, Hwang, Hong, Jeong and colleagues (Seoul National University and others) train VNet-type deep networks on FIRE-2 Milky Way-like simulations to map stellar 3D kinematics to the dark matter density field. They then apply the model to real Gaia DR3 stars to infer the local dark matter distribution. Accepted in MNRAS on Nov 24.

items.title: Queen's researcher uses AI technology behind ChatGPT to reveal hidden solar magnetism
items.excerpt: QUB's Dr Ryan J. Campbell trained a transformer-style AI on a simulated Sun, then applied it to real Sunrise III balloon-telescope data, which it analysed in about four seconds. The model found that weak quiet-Sun magnetic fields mostly run along the surface, a finding an established method confirmed (Astronomy & Astrophysics). Off-list domain, used because no on-list fresh observational-astronomy AI item was found.

items.title: Frozen language model helps predict materials properties with roughly 95% less training time
items.excerpt: ZEBRA-Prop converts material structure and composition into text, embeds it with a frozen MatBERT, and feeds the embeddings to a small network that predicts band gap and formation energy. It cuts training time by about 95% compared with LLM-Prop (Advanced Intelligent Systems).

items.title: Disliking AI doesn't deter its influence
items.source: Phys.org (City St George's, University of London)
items.excerpt: Three financial decision experiments with more than 1,250 participants found that people said they preferred human advisers but followed AI and human advice about equally. Lower trust in AI predicted a stronger stated preference for humans but did not reduce reliance on AI advice (Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin).

items.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
items.excerpt: Google Research uses multi-agent social simulations with fixed hidden motives to test whether LLM assistants can infer a character's motive from a user's subjective account. Social reasoning gets much harder when it is mediated through the user, and models need more detail than humans to reach the right answer.
